blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Multi-bit watermarking embeds a message, typically an account identifier, into LLM output so that harmful text can be traced to its origin. We show an attack technique that allows to alter the watermarking message. This allows to, for example, exchange the embedded account ID to an arbitrary different one. The attacker mainly needs access to a few accounts for generating LLM output and model logits, but crucially not the secret key used to watermark. The attacker then rewrites the text, keeping its meaning, so that the watermarking message decoder recovers the watermarking message embedded by the attacker. We are, to our knowledge, the first to propose such an attack, which we call a targeted displacement. Theoretically, we present upper and lower bounds on the probability of our attack succeeding. This bound depends on the number of accounts the attacker has access to, the length of the message and some characteristics of the given text. Our attack can succeed whenever we can bound the ambiguity of the generated text well enough. Empirically, we test our attack technique against five watermarking methods and four LLMs. Attack success tracks our predicted bounds, allowing us to alter watermarking messages in almost all cases with high accuracy, given enough accounts. Our code can be found at https://github.com/Batorskq/PinIt.
blocks.zh: 多位水标记将一个消息,通常是一个账户标识符,嵌入到LLM输出中,这样有害文本就可以被追溯到它的出处. 我们展示一种攻击技术 允许改变水印信息。 例如,这允许将嵌入式账户ID交换到任意的不同的账户. 攻击者主要需要访问几个账户来生成LLM输出和模型日志,但关键不是用于水印的秘密密钥. 攻击者再重写出文字,保留其意义,使水印信息解码器恢复由攻击者嵌入的水印信息. 据我们所知,我们首先提出这种攻击,我们称之为有针对性的流离失所。 理论上,我们呈现出我们攻击成功概率的上下界限。 此绑定取决于攻击者可以访问的帐号数量,消息的长度以及给定文本的一些特征. 只要我们能够很好地将所产生的文字的模糊性联系在一起,我们的攻击就能够成功。 从经验上讲,我们用5个水标记法和4个LLM来测试攻击技术. 攻击成功追踪到我们预计的界限,使我们能够在几乎所有情况下都以高度准确的方式改变水印信息,并有足够的说明。 我们的代码可以在https://github.com/Batorskq/PinIt上找到.

blocks.en:
Watermarks let a provider recognize text that its language model generated ( Kirchenbauer et al., 2023 ) .
Multi-bit watermarks also hide a message in the text, typically the identifier of the account that requested it, so that a decoder holding the secret key can attribute a harmful text to its account ( Fernandez et al., 2023 ; Yoo et al., 2024 ; Qu et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2026 ) .
We show that an attacker can effectively alter the watermark message (Figure 1 ).
With a few accounts of its own and without the secret key, it rewrites a text that carries a source message m m , keeping its semantics, so that the decoder reads a chosen target message m ′ m^{\prime} , such as the identifier of a third user.
We call this targeted displacement .
Obviously, such a watermarking attack can have serious security and privacy implications, when pinning harmful or sensitive text on an innocent party.
blocks.zh:
Watermarks让一个供应商承认其语言模型生成的文本(Kirchenbauer等人,2023年).
多位水印在文本中也隐藏了一条信息,一般是请求其的账户识别符,这样持有密钥的解码器就可以将有害文本归于其账户(Fernandez等人,2023;Yoo等人,2024;Qu等人,2025;Li等人,2024;Jiang等人,2025;Xu等人,2026).
我们显示攻击者可以有效改变水印信息(图1).
它用自己的几条账号,没有密钥,就重写一个带源消息m m的文本,保留其语义,这样解码器就能读取一个选定的目标消息m ' m^{\prime},例如第三个用户的标识符.
我们称之为有针对性的流离失所。
显然,如果将有害或敏感的文字贴在无辜一方身上,这种水印攻击会造成严重的安全和隐私影响。

blocks.en:
Prior attacks remove the watermark ( Krishna et al., 2023 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) or spoof its presence ( Jovanović et al., 2024 ; Gu et al., 2024 ; Pang et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ) .
They hence change whether the text is recognized as watermarked or not.
That a multi-bit watermark might be steered toward a specific user was anticipated ( Jovanović et al., 2024 ; Gloaguen et al., 2025b ) and stated as a security goal ( Qu et al., 2025 ) , but no known attack, to our knowledge, was able to alter an underlying watermarking message.
We develop the first such attack and a theory of what any such attack can achieve.
blocks.zh:
先前的攻击消除了水印(Krishna等人,2023年;Zhang等人,2024年)或其存在(Jovanović等人,2024年;Gu等人,2024年;Pang等人,2024年;Jiang等人,2025年)。
因此,它们改变了案文是否被确认为水印。
据我们所知,预计可以将多位水印引向特定用户(Jovanović等人,2024年;Gloaguen等人,2025年b),并称这是一个安全目标(Qu等人,2025年),但据我们所知,没有已知的攻击能够改变一个基本的水印信息。
我们发展出第一次这种攻击,以及任何这种攻击能够达到何种目的的理论。

blocks.en:
We study attacks on so called distortion-based watermarking methods, which include popular green-list and red-list methods ( Kirchenbauer et al., 2023 ; Kirchenbauer et al., 2024 ; Zhao et al., 2024 ; Lee et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2024b ; Lu et al., 2024 ) and their multi-bit variants ( Fernandez et al., 2023 ; Yoo et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Qu et al., 2025 ) .
Such schemes make the generator favor, at each step, a subset of the vocabulary that depends on the message and the secret key.
The decoder checks how consistently a text follows the subsets of each candidate message.
The attacker cannot compute these subsets without the key, but a few accounts whose messages are known can reveal enough information about the favored subset.
When comparing an account’s next-token distribution with the base model, we see which tokens are favored, and comparing accounts with one another shows the tokens the target message m ′ m^{\prime} would favor.
A paraphraser restricted to these tokens then rewrites the text (Figure 2 ).
Not every target message is reachable however: when the accounts are too few or their underlying watermark messages are too similar, several targets look the same to the attacker.
For such cases we prove an upper bound on the efficacy of any possible attacker.
Additionally, we provide lower bounds for our attacker:
For any target message m ′ m^{\prime} can compute a certificate, without access to the key, for a lower bound on the probability that the decoder will decode m ′ m^{\prime} .
We evaluate the attack on five published watermarking methods using four LLMs
(Section 4 ).
blocks.zh:
我们研究攻击所谓的扭曲水标记方法,包括流行的绿名单和红名单方法(Kirchenbauer等人,2023年;Kirchenbauer等人,2024年;Zhao等人,2024年;Lee等人,2024年;Lu等人,2024年)及其多位变体(Fernandez等人,2023年;Yoo等人,2024年;Wang等人,2024年;Qu等人,2025年)。
这种方案使得生成器在每一个步骤上都倾向于一个依赖于消息和密钥的词汇子集.
解码器检查一个文本是否始终遵循每个候选信件的子集。
攻击者无法在没有密钥的情况下计算这些子集,但少数消息已知的账号可以透露关于偏好子集的足够信息.
在比较一个账户的下个子分布与基准模型时, 我们可以看到哪些符号是首选的,
一个限定于这些符号的解码器然后重写文本(图2 ).
然而,并不是每个目标信息都可以被达到:当账户太少或者其基本水印信息太相似时,几个目标对攻击者来说看起来是一样的.
对于这种情况,我们证明任何可能的攻击者的效力都有上限。
此外,我们为攻击者提供较低的界限:
对于任何目标消息 m \ m^{\prime } 可以计算一个证书, 不访问密钥, 对于一个下限的概率, 解码器会解码 m \ m^{\prime } 。
我们用四个LLMS来评估五种已公布的水标记方法的攻击
(第4节)

blocks.en:
Our contributions are the following. • To our knowledge, we develop the first attack on a multi-bit watermarking method that can inject arbitrary target messages without access to the key.
Its three steps depend on the scheme. • We give upper bounds on attack success for any attack method on multi-bit watermarking schemes and a lower bound that certifies the probability of attack success for our method. We exactly characterize in closed form reachable target messages. • We evaluate the attack on five published watermarking methods and four LLMs, confirm the bound, show which schemes fall to one account, to multiple colluding accounts, or resist, and measure the price in fidelity for generating watermarked text with a target message.
blocks.zh:

其三个步骤取决于该计划。 我们给攻击成功的上限 任何攻击方法 对于多位水标记方案, 和一个更低的界限 证明攻击成功的概率 我们的方法。 我们完全以封闭的形式描述可达到的目标信息。 我们评估5种公开的标注水的方法和4种LLMs的攻击,确认约束,显示哪些方案属于一个账户,属于多个串联账户,或抵制,并衡量产生标注水的文本与目标信息的价格。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Zero-bit watermarks bias the next-token distribution toward a keyed token
set ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Huo et al., 2024 ; Kirchenbauer et al., 2023 ; Kirchenbauer et al., 2024 ; Lee et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2024b ; Liu and Bu, 2024 ; Lu et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2024 ) ,
sample from it without distortion ( Chen et al., 2025b ; Christ et al., 2024 ; Fu et al., 2024 ; Golowich and Moitra, 2024 ; He et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2024 ; Mao et al., 2025 ; Tsur et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Zhao et al., 2025 ) ,
or select among drafts ( Giboulot and Furon, 2024 ; Hou et al., 2024 ) .
They only detect presence. Multi-bit watermarks, like linguistic
steganography ( Shen et al., 2020 ; Ziegler et al., 2019 ) , hide a
message, typically a user identifier. CycleShift cyclically shifts one keyed
set by the message ( Fernandez et al., 2023 ) , MPAC gives each context a
message position and a vocabulary coloring ( Yoo et al., 2024 ) ,
RSBH spreads a Reed–Solomon codeword over public segments ( Qu et al., 2025 ) , DepthW keys a depth permutation by the whole
code ( Li et al., 2024 ) , StealthInk reweights a keyed
permutation without distortion ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) , and XMark
suppresses keyed vocabulary quarters within public blocks ( Xu et al., 2026 ) . Other schemes edit or paraphrase the text ( Lau et al., 2024 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2022 ; Yoo et al., 2023 ) ,
balance, stack, or symmetrize partitions ( Feng et al., 2025 ; Park et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Zhu et al., 2026 ) ,
correct, verify, or layer the payload ( Chen et al., 2026 ; Kim et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026 ) , personalize it ( An et al., 2026c ; Yu et al., 2025 ) , or serve diffusion LMs, agents, and code
models ( Huang and Wan, 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026b ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) .
Attribution has been formalized ( Jiang et al., 2026 ; Song and Shahabi, 2026 ) , and
CertMark certifies the decoded message ( Batorski et al., 2026 ) . These
works protect the message against erasure by edits and paraphrases. We ask
which messages an attacker can make the decoder read.

blocks.en:
Paraphrasing, editing, translation, and ensembling remove watermarks ( Cheng et al., 2025a ; Cheng et al., 2025b ; Diaa et al., 2025 ; Harel-Canada et al., 2025 ; He et al., 2024 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2026a ; Hwang et al., 2026 ; Krishna et al., 2023 ; Pan et al., 2025 ; Rastogi and Pruthi, 2024 ; Wu et al., 2026b ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) ,
benchmarks compare schemes ( Pan et al., 2024 ; Tu et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2026a ) , and
queries reveal whether and how a model is watermarked ( Gloaguen et al., 2025a ; Liu et al., 2025 ) . Closer to us, stealing estimates a
zero-bit scheme’s keyed sets from queries ( Chen et al., 2025a ; Jovanović et al., 2024 ; Wu and Chandrasekaran, 2024 ) and distillation copies a watermark into another model ( An et al., 2026a ; Gu et al., 2024 ; Sander et al., 2024 ) , so that
an attacker can scrub it or spoof it on any text. Robustness alone permits
piggyback spoofing ( Pang et al., 2024 ) . Defenses harden watermarks against
spoofing or detect it ( An et al., 2025 ; An et al., 2026b ; Gloaguen et al., 2025b ; Liu et al., 2024a ; Shen et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) ,
and image watermarks can likewise be forged or overwritten ( Dong et al., 2025 ; Müller et al., 2025 ; Saberi et al., 2024 ; Senthuran et al., 2026 ; Souček et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2024 ) .
A zero-bit spoof forges one verdict, whereas spoofing a multi-bit watermark could
incriminate a specific user ( Gloaguen et al., 2025b ) , and we study
this attack. Combining outputs under several keys removes a watermark ( Pang et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2026b ) . Our attacker combines accounts under one key
to forge a message, and our symmetry bound limits it as impossibility and
trade-off results limit the defender ( Pratihar and Mukhopadhyay, 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) . The rewrite steers a
paraphraser toward a token set, as in lexically constrained and controlled
decoding ( Dathathri et al., 2020 ; Hu et al., 2019 ; Kajiwara, 2019 ; Liu et al., 2021 ; Lu et al., 2021 ; Mudgal et al., 2024 ; Qin et al., 2022 ; Yang and Klein, 2021 ) ,
also used to obfuscate authorship ( Fisher et al., 2024 ) .

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
Figure 2: Overview of targeted displacement. The attacker wants to rewrite a
text that carries watermark message m m , keeping its meaning, so that the
decoder attributes it to a chosen message m ′ m^{\prime} , without the secret key. It
controls accounts with known messages and, at every context used by the
rewrite, compares an account’s next-token distribution with the base model to
recover the account’s green list (step 1). The recovered green lists are
turned into the target’s green list. This succeeds exactly when the target’s
relative bits are constant within every twin class; otherwise the ambiguity
bound of Theorem 1 caps the success probability
(step 2). A
paraphraser rewrites the source under a token-level constraint toward the
target’s set, and the attacker certifies the rewrite from its own posterior
without the key (step 3), so that the provider’s decoder reads the target
message. Only step 2 depends on the watermark scheme.

blocks.en:
We study targeted displacement : rewriting a text that carries a watermark message m m so that the decoder instead recovers the target message m ′ m^{\prime} .
We first state the attacker’s objective and describe the watermarks we study.
blocks.zh:
我们研究有针对性的迁移:重写一个带有水印的m m的文字,
我们首先说明攻击者的目标,并描述我们研究的水印。

blocks.en:
Let ℳ = { 0 , 1 } L \mathcal{M}=\{0,1\}^{L} be the message space.
Let p K , m p_{K,m} be the next-token distribution for encoding watermarked text with message m m and secret key K K .
Typically m m will be the account identifier of the person generating text.

Otherwise we retain the full vocabulary and use a soft bias sampler .
Choose a δ atk > 0 \delta_{\mathrm{atk}}>0 and let r t ( v ) ∝ p t ( v ) exp ( δ atk 𝟏 { v ∈ G K ( m ′ ) ( z < t } ) . r_{t}(v)\propto p_{t}(v)\exp\!\left(\delta_{\mathrm{atk}}\mathbf{1}\{v\in G^{(m^{\prime})}_{K}(z_{<t}\}\right). (8) Thus τ = 0 \tau=0 forces a target-compatible token whenever possible, while larger τ \tau leaves low-mass contexts closer to the paraphraser.

The decoder relies on distinct context-token pairs for its efficacy.
Since context-token pairs can repeat too often (recall that context-token pairs can reappear due to fixed context length ℓ \ell ), and constrained decoding tends to loop, we block repeated 4-grams ( Paulus et al., 2018 ) .
Algorithm 1 in Appendix B lists the complete attack for binary MPAC.

blocks.en:
We attack five published multi-bit schemes: MPAC ( Yoo et al., 2024 ) , RSBH ( Qu et al., 2025 ) , StealthInk ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) , XMark ( Xu et al., 2026 ) , and CycleShift ( Fernandez et al., 2023 ) . The
watermarked texts are completions of prompts from the RealNewsLike subset of
C4 ( Raffel et al., 2020 ) , written by four generators, Llama-2-7B ( Touvron et al., 2023 ) , Llama-3.1-8B ( Grattafiori et al., 2024 ) ,
Qwen3.5-4B, and Qwen3.5-9B ( Qwen Team, 2026 ) .
The attacker uses the same model as chat model for rewriting.
We measure attack efficacy by the exact-match rate, the fraction of rewrites whose decoded message equals the target, and by bit accuracy.
We compare both metrics with the symmetry upper bound of Theorem 1 in the
binary position–color case, with its scheme-specific counterpart otherwise, and
with the attacker’s certificate ( 15 ).
Appendix C gives the corpora, decoding settings, attack
conditions, the formal definitions of every metric, and the
implementation details.

meets it once the accounts make the target structurally reachable, so each
scheme’s residual ambiguity decides how many accounts it withstands:
CycleShift falls to a
single account, MPAC and StealthInk once the accounts separate every message
position or show every symbol value, XMark once every symbol value has
appeared at every block, and RSBH only to coalitions large enough to cover
its codeword symbols. Message length changes none of this up to 16 bits.
At 32 bits the bound still reaches one, but 200 tokens spread too few votes
over each position for a reliable majority, so success falls short of the
bound until the text grows (Appendix H ), and 64-bit messages
exceed what 200 tokens carry for every scheme. Across schemes, a paraphrase
without watermark knowledge stays at chance.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
Targeted displacement is, to our knowledge, the first attack that steers a multi-bit LLM watermark to a chosen message without the key.
On five published schemes its success meets the predicted upper bound once enough accounts collude.
We argue that our attack can be successfully executed for insiders on closed source LLMs, with potential security implications, including identity theft.

据我们所知,有针对性地迁移是第一次攻击,它将一个多位LLM水印引向一个没有钥匙的选定信息。
在五个公布的计划中,它的成功满足了预测的上限,只要有足够的账户串通。
我们辩称,我们的攻击可以在封闭源代码LLMs上为内幕者成功执行,并可能产生安全影响,包括身份盗窃.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
The limitations of our paper are the assumptions of its threat model. Our
attacker knows the watermarking scheme and its public hyperparameters but
not the secret key. It has the unwatermarked base model and its tokenizer.
It controls accounts whose embedded identifiers it knows, all watermarked
under the provider’s single key, and it reads the next-token distributions
of these accounts at the contexts of its rewrite. These assumptions are,
however, standard in the watermarking literature. That the attacker knows
everything except the key is Kerckhoffs’ principle, which the watermark
stealing threat model adopts explicitly ( Jovanović et al., 2024 ) .
Access to the unwatermarked distribution of the model is the available base
responses setting of the same threat model and of its successors ( Jovanović et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2025a ) , and it is the attacker
against which stealthiness is argued ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) .
Accounts with known identifiers are the spoofing adversary against which
RSBH is argued secure ( Qu et al., 2025 ) , and a single provider
key with the identifier as the message is how every scheme we study embeds
it ( Fernandez et al., 2023 ; Yoo et al., 2024 ; Qu et al., 2025 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2026 ) .
Next-token log-probabilities are returned by public APIs and assumed by
prior attacks ( Pang et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2025a ) . Our attacker reads the
full distribution, which idealizes the top- k k entries that APIs return.
A provider that hides account identifiers, keys the labeling per account,
or withholds log-probabilities removes what the attacker reads, and we do
not measure the query cost of sample access, under which the symmetry bound
still holds.

blocks.en: Ethics Statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en:
This work was conducted in accordance with the ACL Code of Ethics and the
ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct, and we have adhered to the
rules throughout this research. We recognize that the attack we describe
could be misused to make a watermark decoder attribute a harmful text to a
user who did not write it, and that decoded identifiers may feed moderation
or legal decisions. Our intention is to show providers and scheme
designers that attribution by a multi-bit watermark can be displaced
without the key, so that a decoded identifier is not treated as conclusive
evidence on its own and so that future schemes are designed against this
threat. The symmetry bound also tells a provider which targets no attacker can
reach. All experiments use public prompts, open-weight models, and
accounts that we simulate locally, and no deployed service or real user was
involved. We also acknowledge that appropriate safeguards and further
evaluation are necessary to mitigate risks in real world applications.

The attacker rewrites each text with a chat model that shares the
generator’s tokenizer (Llama-2-7B-chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and the Qwen
model itself with its reasoning mode disabled) and has distribution access
to its accounts. The paraphraser samples at temperature 0.7 and top- p p 0.9. We report the constrained rewriting rule of
Section 3.1 with τ = 0 \tau=0 , and the paraphraser
additionally blocks repeated 4-grams, which keeps constrained decoding from
collapsing into loops. Conditions: the own account with the target set to
the complement m ¯ \bar{m} or to a message one bit away, and n n colluding
accounts with a uniformly random target. Fact protection
(used in the fidelity experiments of Appendix J ) leaves a
step unconstrained when the
paraphraser’s top token has probability at least κ \kappa and ends the text,
is whitespace, or continues a numeral, name, or negation copied from the
source. Such a token may vote against the target, and the certificate counts
it as a rival vote.

Every generation, attack, and scoring job runs on one NVIDIA H100 (94 GB)
or A40 (48 GB) of a Slurm cluster with 8 CPU cores and 64 GB of host
memory (96 GB for the judges); the LLM judges run on two A40s with tensor
parallelism and the NLI and NER scorers on one A40 (wall-clock costs in
Appendix I ). The code is Python 3.12 with PyTorch 2.11 ( Paszke et al., 2019 ) and Transformers 5.10 ( Wolf et al., 2020 ) , except that the earliest Llama-2-7B
MPAC runs at 8 and 16 bits with τ = 10 − 3 \tau=10^{-3} used PyTorch 2.4.1 and
Transformers 4.45.2; the judges are served by vLLM 0.23 ( Kwon et al., 2023 ) . The generators are the Hugging Face checkpoints Llama-2-7b-hf , Llama-3.1-8B , Qwen3.5-4B , and Qwen3.5-9B , and the paraphrasers Llama-2-7b-chat-hf , Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct , and the two Qwen models themselves, so one
copy of a Qwen model serves as generator, attacker’s base model, and
paraphraser. Llama-2-7B generates in float16 and the other generators in
bfloat16; during the attack every model runs in bfloat16, the Llama
paraphrasers use eager attention, a guard replaces non-finite logits during
rewriting (Llama-2-7B-chat produced NaNs in batched float16 generation),
and the learner compares log-probabilities in float32.

blocks.en:
Corpora are sampled in batches of 10 prompts, truncated to 1,200 tokens
and left-padded, with exactly T T new tokens, top- k k disabled, and a
5-gram repetition block ( Paulus et al., 2018 ) ; the unwatermarked
completion of a prompt reuses the sampling seed of its watermarked twin.
Rewrites are sampled in batches of 8 with top- k k disabled. The 4-gram
block of Tables 1 and 4 and of
Figure 7 is the no_repeat_ngram_size option
of Transformers, which indexes the prompt as well, so a rewrite repeats no
4-gram of its source; the rewrite-only block of Appendix J is our own logits processor over the generated tokens. The watermarked API
is simulated in-process: an oracle takes the generator’s logits at the
attacker’s prefix, applies the watermark of the queried account (the δ \delta bias of its set, or StealthInk’s reweighting), and returns the full
log-softmax; the base-model forward pass is shared with the attacker’s own
call and cached per prefix. For the additive schemes the learner
classifies every token of the vocabulary by thresholding the log-ratio log ⁡ p i ​ ( v ∣ c ) − log ⁡ p ⁡ ( v ∣ c ) \log p_{i}(v\mid c)-\log p(v\mid c) , which equals δ 1 { v ∈ G i ( c ) } − log Z \delta\,\mathbf{1}\{v\in G_{i}(c)\}-\log Z up to float32 rounding, at the
midpoint of its range; StealthInk uses the closed-form rule of
Appendix A . Learned sets are cached per context
and account, and for MPAC accounts whose learned sets agree on at least 90
percent of the jointly resolved tokens form one twin class. Each corpus
carries a pool of extra accounts with random messages (16 for MPAC at 8 and
16 bits, up to 128 for the longer messages and for the schemes with more
positions); the n n colluding accounts are the attacker’s own account and
the first n − 1 n-1 accounts of one fixed random ordering of the pool, so the
coalitions are nested in n n , and the target of a text is drawn by a
generator seeded with the condition, the global seed, and the text index,
so a text faces the same target under every rewrite rule. The certificate
( 15 ) uses 1,000 Monte Carlo draws of the
position assignment for MPAC, 300 for RSBH and StealthInk, and 200 for
XMark, and is exact for CycleShift. Scheme parameters follow the released
code: δ = 2 \delta=2 wherever a logit bias is added (StealthInk reweights
without a bias), one-token contexts except for XMark (two tokens) and
StealthInk (three), and set fractions γ = 1 / 2 \gamma=1/2 for MPAC and RSBH, 1 / 4 1/4 for CycleShift, and 9 / 16 9/16 for XMark. Our MPAC re-implementation
draws the position and the color partition of a context from a PRNG
seeded by a hash of key and context rather than from torch.randperm , so that generation and detection agree across
devices; an 8-bit corpus generated with the released MPAC code and judged
by its detector gives the same success rates as our re-implementation.
The other schemes keep the seeding and decoding of their released code
(Appendix A ), with a secret key where the released
code uses a fixed constant.

blocks.en: Appendix I Runtime
blocks.zh: 附录一 运行时间

blocks.en:
Every attack job rewrites the 100 texts of one corpus under every condition
of its row in Figure 7 on a single NVIDIA H100 (94 GB), with the generator, the paraphraser, and the attacker’s copy of the
base model loaded together and batches of 8 texts. The API is simulated
locally with the generator itself, so the time includes the oracle’s own
forward passes. Table 5 reports, for the settings run on the H100, the
wall-clock time per rewritten text under the τ = 0 \tau=0 rule, including
decoding, the certificate, and the learner’s queries. The τ = 10 − 3 \tau=10^{-3} rule costs the same. The
dominant cost is one base-model forward pass per new context, so schemes
whose context is longer than one token (XMark, StealthInk) query at almost
every step, while MPAC, CycleShift, and RSBH reuse contexts. Queries is the
number of oracle calls per rewritten text with a plan, one per context and
account whose set the learner resolved, and corpus is the time to sample the 100
watermarked and 100 unwatermarked continuations of a corpus.

blocks.en:
Assumption (A1) is a distributional requirement, not a consequence of
the algebraic identity ( 33 ) alone. In the binary
position–color idealization, at each context the position is uniform
on [ L ] [L] and the balanced two-color partition is uniform, independently
of that position and of the assignments at other contexts. A position
permutation and per-position color flips define a bijection of the
possible (position, partition) pairs. Each pair originally has the same
probability, so the relabeled pair is again uniform. The transformation
acts separately at each context, preserving independence across
contexts, and repeated contexts still read the same assignment.
This proves invariance of the entire ideal key table. For a concrete
finite-seed pseudorandom implementation, a uniform seed by itself does
not prove that the induced table distribution has this exact symmetry.
The information-theoretic conclusion above uses (A1).

For a released decoder with a label-dependent tie rule, apply the theorem

and the presence of an acceptance threshold alone does not establish this.

We prove Theorem 2 for a fixed observation O O and rewrite z z . In the ideal-key model, the hidden positions J K ​ ( c ) J_{K}(c) are initially independent and uniform on [ L ] [L] across distinct
contexts. The controlled-account sets observed at c c reveal the account
signature x J K ​ ( c ) x_{J_{K}(c)} , and therefore the twin class T ⁡ ( c ) T(c) , but not the
position inside that class. The within-class symmetries proved in
Appendix K assign equal posterior probability to every
position in T ⁡ ( c ) T(c) . Independence across distinct contexts is preserved
because the ideal key assigns them independently and the observations expose
only their classes, and repeated occurrences of the same context share the same
assignment. If no class was identified, the observation gives no position
information and the posterior remains uniform on [ L ] [L] . Consequently, the
conditional law of the position map J K J_{K} on the contexts of z z is exactly Π O \Pi_{O} .

blocks.en:
The certificate of Section 3.2 evaluates the decoder’s
vote tally exactly under the attacker’s posterior. The following bound
complements it from the other side: it lower-bounds the success probability
in terms of the true vote counts and vote biases, which the attacker cannot
see, and explains why the constrained rule succeeds once enough contexts
carry a target vote. We fix the setting with numbered assumptions, state
the bound, and prove it in four steps: the vote probabilities of the two
rewriting rules, the decoder’s success as an intersection of per-position
majority events, Hoeffding’s inequality for each failure event, and a union
bound over the positions.

blocks.en:
This appendix works through two relabelings of a binary position–color
watermark. The first survives after the controlled-account messages are
known and therefore lies in ℋ M \mathcal{H}_{M} , while the second is a valid symmetry of
the watermark, but is ruled out by those messages. Both are pure position
relabelings: their per-position color-flip vector is zero.
